title: Remove global epoch lock: introduce lease-less batcher and KV gradualizer
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Triage and implement a replacement for the monolithic global epoch lock used by the continuous batching controller. Introduce a lease-less batch coordinator to remove global contention and a "KV gradualizer" to perform safe, low-latency migrations of cache shards and metadata without global quiesce. Goal: reduce tail latency spikes under bursty ingress and unlock more parallelism for multi-tenant workloads.
background: Current serving runtime relies on a global epoch lock to coordinate batch windows and KV cache GC. This lock serializes a number of control-plane operations (slot rebalance, epoch bump, shard compaction) and has repeatedly shown up on perf flamegraphs as a contention hotspot during sustained bursts and during model swaps. Prior attempts at targeted refactors reduced some pain but left a global serialization point. This ticket scopes the next step: remove the global epoch lock and replace its guarantees with a combination of lightweight per-shard leases and an incremental, lazily-applied migration for KV state.
technical_design:
High-level components:
1) Lease-less batch coordinator: a cooperative batch formation protocol based on per-lane soft-leases and token windows. Peers advertise token availability and negotiate commit responsibilities without a global epoch barrier. Uses optimistic commit + short abort/retry on conflict.
2) KV Gradualizer: background process that migrates KV metadata and slab ownership incrementally. Migration tasks are small (sub-100ms) and bounded; a per-shard migration cursor is kept in durable metadata to resume work. Hotkeys are detected and pinned during migration to avoid thrashing.
3) Compatibility shim: maintain a temporary compatibility layer where epoch bump RPCs are translated to lease-renew messages so older nodes remain interoperable during rollout.
4) Observability and SLOs: expose metrics for lease failures, migration throughput, per-tenant tail latency, and abort/retry rates. Add tracing spans for batch negotiation.

Implementation notes:
- Files touched: batch/coordinator/*, kvcache/migration/*, metadata/lease_store.go, rpc/compat_epoch_bridge.go
- Use existing allocator primitives (slot-channels) but eliminate the global epoch heartbeat path.
- Keep deterministic fallback: if lease negotiation fails for N retries, route the work to a conservative single-allocator path (existing epoch path) for correctness.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch with unit + integration tests, toggle behind runtime flag 'lease_mode_v2'.
2) Canary on internal staging: enable for low-traffic region, observe lease metrics and migration throughput for 48 hours.
3) Gradual ramp: enable for 10% of requests in production with aggressive alerting. Migrate one shard group at a time.
4) If tail latency or lease-retry rate exceeds thresholds, flip back to legacy epoch path and collect full traces for root cause.
5) Final cutover once migration throughput reaches target and abort rates are <0.1% for 72h.
acceptance_criteria: No loss of correctness: requests that would have succeeded under the old epoch system must succeed after migration or fall back deterministically.
Tail P95/P99 token generation latency improvement of at least 15% under synthetic burst workloads compared to baseline runtime-1.21.
KV migration not increasing 99th percentile KV read latency by more than 10ms during steady-state.
Observability: lease-failure-rate < 0.5% and migration throughput metrics available in Grafana dashboard 'runtime.kv.gradualizer'.
Rollout toggle 'lease_mode_v2' implemented and tested for safe rollback.
test_plan: Unit tests for conflict/retry logic and migration resume behavior. Integration test harness simulating 1000 concurrent short-lived sessions with randomized hotkey distribution. Load test on perf lab that reproduces high burst-factor (x50 arrival rate) and measures tail latency. Chaos test: kill coordinator nodes during migrations to validate resume correctness.
